newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans to launch 7 US-made probes on June 18.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans to launch 7 US-made probes on June 18.

text.p: Russia plans to launch seven U.S.-made satellites next week for a space communications network being set up by an American consortium, a military space forces spokesman said on Wednesday.
Sergei Gorbunov told Reuters the probes would be sent into orbit for the Iridium LLC consortium on June 18 at 8.00 p.m. Moscow time (1600 GMT) from Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
"The booster and satellites are having pre-launch tests at Baikonur according to the schedule," Gorbunov said. The launch will use a heavy Proton booster owned by Russian rocket maker Khrunichev.
Khrunichev space centre spokesman Konstantin Lantratov said that it would be the first of three Proton launches for the Iridium satellites.
The second launch is scheduled for September and the third for early next year. The three launches will cost an estimated $179 million.
The first five probes were launched in May on a U.S. Delta rocket, marking the start of a project by Iridium to group 66 satellites in the low Earth orbit.
Khrunichev has invested $80 million of its own funds in the project, which will provide former Soviet republics with cellular phone communications, Lantratov said.
Iridium LLC is a consortium including Iridium World Communications Ltd, Motorola Inc, Sprint Corp, Lockheed Martin Corp and Raytheon Co.
